prompt: A voltage record alternates equally between positive and negative values of the same nonzero size. Its mean meter reads zero. Which interpretation is sound?

options.explanation: Positive and negative values can cancel in the mean even while the signal continues to fluctuate.

options.text: Its RMS must also be zero because signs cancel
options.explanation: RMS squares values first, so negative values do not cancel positive ones.

options.text: Its RMS can reveal a nonzero level despite zero mean
options.explanation: Correct. Mean describes signed offset; RMS retains the nonzero contribution of both signs.

workedExample:
1. Equal positive and negative values cancel when averaged with their signs.
2. Squaring makes both contributions positive.
3. The RMS is therefore nonzero and remains measured in volts after the square root.

link.title: Primary source: The Scientist and Engineer’s Guide to DSP

prompt: A sensor record contains fluctuations plus a nonzero constant offset. You subtract this record’s mean. Which statement describes its centred RMS?

options.text: It measures the remaining fluctuations around the removed mean
options.explanation: Correct. Subtracting the mean centres the record and removes its offset contribution from RMS.

options.text: It must be zero because the centred mean is zero
options.explanation: Zero mean does not remove fluctuations or make their squared values cancel.

options.text: It still includes the same constant offset contribution
options.explanation: The constant offset represented by the record mean was subtracted from every sample.

workedExample:
1. The original RMS includes both offset and fluctuations.
2. Subtracting the record mean removes that record’s constant offset.
3. The remaining RMS describes the centred fluctuations. Whether removing that offset is useful depends on what the sensor is meant to measure.

link.title: Primary source: The Scientist and Engineer’s Guide to DSP

prompt: Which conclusions are safe? Select all that apply.

options.text: A zero mean proves every sample is zero
options.explanation: Positive and negative samples can cancel in the mean.

options.text: RMS of a voltage record is measured in volts
options.explanation: Correct. The square root restores the input unit.

options.text: A short record’s mean need not equal a permanent sensor bias
options.explanation: Correct. Record boundaries and changing signals affect the average.

workedExample:
1. Check what each statistic actually computes.
2. Mean can cancel signs; RMS cannot cancel their squares.
3. RMS retains voltage units, while interpreting a measured mean as permanent bias requires knowledge beyond that short record.

link.title: Primary source: The Scientist and Engineer’s Guide to DSP
